rules.title: Application screening fee capped at actual costs and $30 (CPI-adjusted)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee no higher than its actual out-of-pocket costs, and never more than $30 per applicant, adjusted yearly for CPI since 1998. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund any unused portion, give you a copy of your credit report within 7 days, and cannot charge a fee if no unit is or will soon be available.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) and their agents receiving rental applications in California; applicants include guarantors and cosigners.
rules.exemptions: Does not preempt deposit and fee rules under federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.

rules.title: Screening fee allowed only with first-come process or refund to applicants not selected
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee only if it either (A) considers completed applications in the order received, using written criteria, approves the first qualified applicant, and charges only applicants whose applications it actually considers, or (B) refunds the full fee to every applicant not selected, within 7 days of choosing a tenant or 30 days after the application, whichever comes first.
rules.key_value: Refund within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission, whichever first
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords and their agents collecting application screening fees for California residential rentals.
rules.exemptions: No refund is needed under option A for an applicant denied after consideration for failing the landlord's written screening criteria.

notes: The effective date of 2026-01-01 comes from the history note for the latest amendment (Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, AB 1170). The $30 cap itself dates back much earlier: the text adjusts it for CPI starting 1998-01-01. This document doesn't say when the subdivision (c)(2) process/refund rule was first added, so I used the current version's date. I split § 1950.6 into two records: the fee cap with its receipt, refund and credit-report duties, and the requirement to use a first-come process or refund applicants who aren't selected. A reviewer could reasonably merge them into one. The document doesn't give the current CPI-adjusted dollar amount or any penalty.
